title: Judge a Misbehaving Delivery
scenario: It is 6:18 AM. Today's file honors the column contract - and still manages to misbehave four different ways. Before the cleaning step runs, judge each anomaly: which are contract violations, which are just mess, and which demand a check before anything consumes them.
input:
hub, peak, settled
ercot , $204/MWh, $151/MWh
ERCOT, $204/MWh, $151/MWh
spp, 98.5 /MWh, $90/MWh
MISO, $77/MWh,
waue, $63/MWh, $58/MWh

Feed contract: columns hub, peak, settled; one reading per hub per night; every column populated. WAUE was added to the desk last month.
instructions: Compare each row against the stated contract.
Validate to record the delivery assessment.

questions.prompt: Two identical ERCOT rows arrived. What happened, and what must cleaning do?

options.text: One reading was delivered twice - deduplicate, or every sum and average downstream double-counts
Two different ERCOT markets reported - keep both rows
The vendor emphasized an important price - keep both for safety

questions.explain: The contract says one reading per hub per night. Identical values under the same key are a double delivery, and duplicates silently corrupt any aggregate.

questions.prompt: The MISO row has an empty settled column. Is the contract violated?

options.text: Yes - a required column is unpopulated, so the whole row is untrustworthy
Only if more than one cell is blank

questions.explain: The contract requires every column populated. One missing required value poisons the row: its other values may be fine, but the row can no longer be consumed as a complete reading.

questions.prompt: WAUE appears in the feed. What must be checked before downstream steps consume it?

options.text: Nothing - new rows are automatically safe
Whether its prices are higher than ERCOT's
Whether the reference data (forecast, prior day) knows this key yet

questions.explain: A new key in one dataset is a join risk everywhere else. WAUE is valid in the feed - the question is whether the comparisons downstream have anything to join it TO.

questions.prompt: SPP's peak reads 98.5. What kind of value is that?

options.text: A valid decimal number - coercion must preserve it, not round it
An error - prices are always whole numbers
A percentage that slipped into the wrong column

questions.explain: Nothing in the contract says integers. Decimals are ordinary numeric values; the cleaning step's job is to preserve precision, not to tidy it away.

deliveryAssessment.contractViolation: MISO settled column empty - row untrustworthy
deliveryAssessment.newKeyRisk: WAUE - verify references know the key
deliveryAssessment.validButMessy: SPP 98.5 decimal, casing drift, stray spaces - coerce, preserve precision

copilotPrompt: Assess this delivery against its contract: classify the duplicate row, the empty required column, the never-before-seen hub key, and the decimal value - which are violations, which are mess, which are join risks.
successMessage: Delivery judged. The cleaning step now knows exactly which anomaly gets which treatment.

intro.heading: Before you judge: not all anomalies are equal

sections.title: Four anomalies, three verdicts
sections.body: Today's file contains a duplicate (dedupe it), a contract violation (distrust the row), a new key (check the joins), and honest mess (coerce it). Treating them all the same - or all differently by mood - is how pipelines rot.

sections.title: Contracts define violations
sections.body: Whether a blank cell is a problem is not a matter of taste: the contract says every column populated, so it is a violation. Judgment at this tier means citing the contract, not squinting at the file.

sections.title: New keys are everyone else's problem
sections.body: WAUE is perfectly valid HERE. The risk lives downstream, where forecast and baseline data may not know the key yet. Spotting cross-dataset consequences of a local change is a real reviewer's skill.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd download the overnight price file (a CSV or an emailed attachment) and load its rows into a table the workflow can read.

bestFit.how: 'When a file is created' on the feed folder, then Excel 'List rows in a table'
a Cron trigger plus a Read Binary File node when the vendor drops on a schedule

takeaway.heading: Delivery assessed
points: You classified four anomalies into their correct treatments instead of one-size-fits-all suspicion.
You judged the blank cell by the contract, not by intuition - that is what makes the judgment repeatable.
You flagged the new key as a downstream join risk before any join broke.
The medium cleaning lesson executes exactly these verdicts: dedupe ERCOT, drop MISO, keep 98.5, carry WAUE.
The workflow can now triage a misbehaving delivery into violations, mess, and risks - each with its own response.
